assistant|strat_body_construction: Stratocaster has a contoured, beveled body with a bolt-on neck made of alder, ash, or mahogany
assistant|les_paul_body_construction: Les Paul has a single-cutaway mahogany body with a set-in neck and a carved maple top
assistant|strat_neck_specs: Stratocaster has a bolt-on maple neck with a 25.5" scale length and a 22-fret fingerboard
assistant|les_paul_neck_specs: Les Paul has a set-in mahogany neck with a 24.75" scale length and a 22-fret fingerboard
assistant|strat_electronics: Stratocaster has three single-coil pickups with a 5-way switch, master volume, and tone controls
assistant|les_paul_electronics: Les Paul has two humbucker pickups with a 3-way toggle switch and individual volume and tone controls for each pickup
assistant|strat_tone_profile: Stratocaster tone is brighter, snappier, and more articulate with a wide tonal range from single-coils and 5-way switch
assistant|les_paul_tone_profile: Les Paul tone is warmer, fuller, with more sustain, strong midrange, and slightly darker due to humbuckers
assistant|les_paul_weight_range: Les Paul typically weighs around 9-10 pounds
assistant|les_paul_associated_genres: Les Paul is commonly used for rock, blues, heavy metal, hard rock, classic rock, glam metal, and southern rock
assistant|les_paul_fingerpicking_assessm: Les Paul can play acoustic-like fingerpicking but its thick tone, sustain, higher action, and wider neck make it less than ideal
assistant|les_paul_fingerpicking_tips: Tips for fingerpicking on a Les Paul: lighter touch, neck pickup, lighter string gauges, acoustic simulator pedal
assistant|open_d_tuning_notes: Open D tuning is DADF#AD (low to high)
assistant|standard_tuning_notes: Standard tuning is EADGBE (low to high)
assistant|open_d_vs_standard_intervals: Standard tuning uses mixed perfect fourths and major thirds; open D uses primarily perfect fifths
assistant|open_d_chord_shapes: Open D tuning has simpler, more consistent chord shapes, often a single shape for many chords
assistant|open_d_tone_character: Open D tone is warmer and more resonant, focused on lower midrange and bass; standard tuning is brighter
assistant|open_d_slide_suitability: Open D tuning is well-suited for slide guitar; standard tuning is less conducive to it
assistant|open_d_string_gauge_advice: For open D on Les Paul, use heavier strings (0.012-0.052 or 0.013-0.056) for fuller, more resonant tone
assistant|open_d_amp_settings: For open D on Les Paul: gain around 5-6, boost bass at 100-150 Hz, cut mids at 500-800 Hz, reduce treble at 5k-8k Hz
assistant|open_d_setup_tips: For open D: adjust action and intonation, lower pickup height, use neck pickup, add compression, use relaxed right-hand technique
assistant|coil_tap_benefit_open_d: Coil-tap or coil-splitting on a Les Paul adds tonal options useful in open D: brighter tones to cut through, plus warmth and sustain
assistant|les_paul_coil_tap_models: Les Paul models with coil-tap/split features: Standard (coil-tap on tone controls), Traditional (coil-splitting), Custom (often coil-tap or coil-split)
assistant|guitar_purchase_advice: Advised trying out both the Stratocaster and Les Paul before purchase to see which feels and sounds like home
